title: Mujaddara (Rice and Lentils with Crispy Onions)
summary: Onions fried crisp from cold, lentils parboiled, and soaked basmati toasted in the onion oil with warm spices, then cooked together and finished with the onions.
equipment: large heavy casserole (Dutch oven) with lid
2 rimmed trays lined with kitchen paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, for the lentil water
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Fry the onions from cold
steps.text: Put the onions and 375 ml oil in the casserole and set it over high heat. Cook for 25-30 min, stirring often and more frequently as they start to colour, until deep golden. Starting cold lets the onions release their water slowly so they crisp evenly.

steps.title: Drain and keep the oil
steps.text: Tip the onions into the colander set over a bowl, then spread them on a lined tray so they stay crisp. Keep 3 tbsp of the onion-flavoured oil for the rice.

steps.title: Parboil the lentils
steps.text: Simmer the lentils in 1000 ml water with 0.5 tsp salt over low heat for 15-17 min, until just tender but still holding their shape. Drain; they finish cooking with the rice.

steps.title: Soak and rinse the rice
steps.text: Soak the rice in hot water for 15 min, then swish and change the water 4-5 times until it runs almost clear. Washing off surface starch is what keeps the grains separate.

steps.title: Toast with the spices
steps.text: Wipe out the casserole, then heat the 3 tbsp onion oil with the garlic and all the spices over medium heat for 2 min. Add the drained rice and stir for 3 min, until the grain edges turn translucent.

steps.title: Cook and rest
steps.text: Add the 540 ml water, sugar and 0.75 tsp salt, bring to the boil and stir in the lentils. Cover and cook on low for 12 min, then take it off the heat, lay the tea towel under the lid and rest for 10 min.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Fork two-thirds of the onions and the parsley through the rice and lentils. Heap the remaining crispy onions on top just before serving.

tips: Pulling the onions too early is the usual mistake; they crisp only once deep golden, and they darken quickly at the end, so stir constantly then.
Do not throw away the onion oil; it carries much of the flavour.
Use brown or green lentils, which hold their shape; red lentils turn to mush.
Serve with plain yoghurt and a chopped salad.
storage: Refrigerate the rice and lentils promptly and covered up to 3 days; store the onions separately at room temperature in an airtight box for 2 days. Reheat rice only once, covered with a splash of water, until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
